chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the fitrah (small cloth used for wiping after urination), if you set it aside while you are seeking a place for it or waiting for a man (to use it), there is no harm in it.

key_terms.الفِطرَة: A small cloth or stone used for wiping after urination in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.عَزَلتَهَا: You set it aside / separated it
key_terms.فَلَا بَأسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to set aside the fitrah cloth while looking for a place to keep it?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to address the practical concerns of ritual purity (*taharah*) in daily life. It establishes that temporarily setting aside the *fitrah* while seeking a clean spot or waiting for a companion does not break one's state of purity, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (*yusr*) in matters of worship.
